problems.title: By hand
hints: Exclusive: the sum of everything strictly before.

problems.title: Two trees, counted
problems.statement: Scans of n elements (n a power of two).
hints: Round k of Hillis–Steele: every element at index ≥ 2^k adds.
Up-sweep is a reduction (n − 1); the down-sweep does as many.
problems.solution: Hillis–Steele does $\sum_k (n - 2^k) = n\log_2 n - (n-1)$: 129 for 32 and 9,217 for 1,024. Blelloch: $2(n-1)$: 62 and 2,046. For a warp, Hillis–Steele's 5 rounds with all lanes busy beat Blelloch's 10 half-empty rounds; for a 1,024-element block, Blelloch does 4.5× less work.

problems.title: Scan traffic
problems.statement: Exclusive scan of $2^{25}$ 32-bit ints on the GW-1.

parts.prompt: Reduce-then-scan (3n accesses): time bound, in ms?
Speedup of the single-pass design, at best?

problems.solution: (a) 0.786 ms, (b) 0.524 ms, (c) 1.5×. That 1.5× is what decoupled look-back buys, and why CUB uses it.

problems.title: A block scan, composed
problems.statement: A 256-thread block scans one value per thread: warp scans with shuffles, warp totals to shared memory, one warp scans the 8 totals, then each thread adds its warp's offset. Every input is 1.
hints: One barrier after writing totals, one after scanning them.

problems.title: Segmented scan
problems.statement: Values [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], segment-head flags [1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1]. An inclusive segmented scan restarts at each head.
problems.solution: Result [1, 3, 6, 4, 9, 6]. A segmented scan is an ordinary scan with the operator $(f_1, v_1) \oplus (f_2, v_2) = (f_1 \lor f_2,\ f_2 ? v_2 : v_1 + v_2)$, which is associative, so every tree in this chapter applies. It's how sparse matrix–vector products and many graph algorithms run on GPUs.

problems.title: Scan with max
problems.solution: [3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 9, 9, 9]. Any associative operator works; max-scan finds running maxima (record highs, the online-softmax running max).

problems.title: Scanning the tile sums
problems.statement: $2^{25}$ elements in tiles of 2,048; one 256-thread block scans the tile sums, 8 per thread per chunk.

parts.prompt: Chunks the single block walks through?

problems.solution: 16,384 tile sums, 8 chunks of 2,048, carrying the running total between chunks. This is the bug Lab 3's reference had to fix: one chunk handles only 2,048 tiles.

problems.title: Which scan for allocation?
problems.statement: Each thread produces a variable number of outputs.

parts.prompt: Each thread's first output slot is…
options: the inclusive scan of the counts at that thread
the exclusive scan of the counts at that thread
the thread index times the maximum count

problems.solution: The exclusive scan: everything produced by earlier threads. The inclusive scan gives the end of each thread's range, and the last inclusive value is the total size to allocate.

problems.title: Scan as a building block
problems.statement: Radix sort's scatter step, for one 1-bit digit (a split): keys with bit 0 go first, keys with bit 1 after them, both stably. Bits of 8 keys: [1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0].
hints: Zeros: position = exclusive scan of the zero flags. Ones: total zeros + exclusive scan of the one flags.
problems.solution: Zero flags [0,1,1,0,0,1,0,1] scan to [0,0,1,2,2,2,3,3]; there are 4 zeros. One flags [1,0,0,1,1,0,1,0] scan to [0,1,1,1,2,3,3,4]. Key 3 (a one, with 1 one before it) goes to 4 + 1 = 5; key 5 (a zero with 2 zeros before it) to 2. A split is two scans, and a radix sort is a sequence of splits.
